verdict.rationale: Vercel documents its own isolated test surfaces: automatic preview environments for testing changes before production, per-environment variables separating preview from production config, and Vercel Sandbox microVMs for agent-generated code. Vercel Agent also uses secure sandboxes to validate changes before they reach production. However, no evidence explicitly guarantees that preview or sandbox runs are kept off production data; that depends on the user pointing each environment at separate data stores. Neon branching is a marketplace partner capability and earns no credit. Missing for 10: an explicit documented guarantee of production-data isolation for preview or sandbox runs, first-party test-data or seeded-database provisioning, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: automatic preview environments for testing changes before production
Manage local, preview, production, and custom environments and the variables each one uses.
Run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs. Use Vercel Sandbox for agent workflows, debugging, and one-off commands.
It can use secure sandboxes to reproduce issues, validate generated code, and run checks before suggested changes reach production.
